verse.text: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

reflection.scripture: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.
reflection.observation: John 1:14 is one of the most profound declarations in all of Scripture. The eternal Word—who was with God and was God from the beginning—did not remain distant or abstract. He became flesh. He entered our world, our pain, our limitations. The Greek word for 'made his dwelling' (eskēnōsen) literally means 'tabernacled' among us, echoing how God's presence dwelt with Israel in the wilderness. This is not a remote deity but a God who draws near. And what did we see in this nearness? Glory—not the glory of power or spectacle, but the glory of grace and truth intertwined. Not grace without truth (which becomes permissive sentimentality), not truth without grace (which becomes cold legalism), but both, perfectly balanced in the person of Jesus.
reflection.application: Today, consider where you need to 'tabernacle'—to dwell intentionally—with the people God has placed in your life. In a world that increasingly interacts through screens and distance, who needs your physical, emotional, spiritual presence? Where are you tempted to offer grace without truth, or truth without grace? Ask Jesus to show you one relationship where you can embody both today. And remember: the same Word who became flesh now lives in you by His Spirit. You are a dwelling place of God's presence.
reflection.prayer: Father, thank You for not remaining at a distance. Thank You for becoming flesh, for entering our mess, for making Your dwelling among us. Help me to be a dwelling place of Your presence today. Teach me to hold grace and truth together as Jesus did. Show me who needs my nearness today—not my advice from afar, but my presence up close. In Jesus' name, Amen.
